study.title.value: Scheduled Screen Breaks and Eye Discomfort in Adults With Frequent Digital Screen Use: A Randomized Prospective Behavioral Study.

study.background.value: The study asks whether a scheduled break routine changes eye discomfort during frequent screen use compared with usual break habits. A benefit is uncertain. No prior treatment-effect estimate or bibliography is supplied.

value: Estimate the between-group difference in change in average eye-discomfort rating from Day 0 to Day 56 after randomization.

study.hypothesis.value: The scheduled-break group will have a greater reduction in eye discomfort than the usual-habits group. This is an exploratory feasibility study, not a confirmatory efficacy study; benefit is not established.

design.study_design.value: Study type for protocol selection: Prospective. Registry study classification: Interventional. Primary purpose: Supportive Care. Allocation: Randomized. Intervention model: Parallel Assignment. Two groups. Masking: Single, Outcomes Assessor. Participants and the training coordinator know assignment. The clinic vision assessor is masked. This is not a double-masked study; participant-reported symptoms cannot be masked. Number of sites: 2, both in the United States. Condition: Eye discomfort associated with frequent digital screen use. Intervention category: Behavioral. No study-assigned drug, device or surgery. The research assigns a break routine after consent and eligibility confirmation; it does not merely observe a routine chosen before enrollment. Group 1: Scheduled screen breaks, target 36 participants. Group 2: Usual screen-break habits, target 36 participants. Total enrollment: 72 unique people, target 36 per site and 36 per group overall. value.time_frame: Day 0 to Day 56 +/- 7 days after randomization

value: No visual acuity test, satisfaction rating, new training or specimen collection occurs by telephone.

Both groups complete one paper diary entry each evening from the day after randomization (Day 1) through Day 56 inclusive, about two minutes per day. Each entry records total screen-use hours and whether screen use occurred. Scheduled-break participants additionally record the number of eligible 30-minute intervals and the number followed by a completed two-minute break. Usual-habits participants record the number of breaks they naturally took; they are not given adherence targets. An evening entry is not a clinic visit. Day 0 has no home-diary entry. risks_benefits.compensation_or_reimburse.value: Participant compensation: None. No attendance payments, bonus or gift cards. Travel reimbursement only: actual parking or public-transit expenses up to $25 for each of the three attended in-person visits, with receipts; maximum $75 across those visits. statistics.analysis_plan.value: Analysis population: all randomized participants with relevant observed data, analyzed in their assigned group regardless of adherence. Report disposition, withdrawal and missing data by group and site. No automatic exclusion for masking breaches or changes in ordinary care; describe those events. Primary analysis: linear model of Day 56 minus Day 0 symptom change including group, Day 0 symptom score and site. Report adjusted mean change by group and the scheduled-break minus usual-habits adjusted difference with 95% confidence interval. A negative between-group difference favors scheduled breaks. Summarize continuous observations with count, mean, standard deviation, median and range, categorical observations as counts and percentages with explicit denominators. Summarize secondary outcomes descriptively by assigned group, except intervention adherence which is intervention-group-only. Use available observations; do not impute missing symptoms or diaries. Report completeness and missing reasons. No multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory claims or causal certainty is justified by this feasibility study.

design.study_design_summary: Two-site prospective randomized behavioral study, 1:1 parallel assignment to scheduled screen breaks or usual habits. Clinic vision assessor masked; participants and training coordinator unmasked.
design.intervention_description: The training coordinator gives scheduled-break participants a printed sheet and a ten-minute explanation at Day 0: take a two-minute break away from the screen after each 30 minutes of screen use during screen-use sessions lasting at least two hours. No app, timer or screen device is supplied or tested. Usual-habits participants continue their ordinary break habits; they are not instructed to avoid breaks. Both groups may continue ordinary eye care.
design.randomization: After written consent, eligibility confirmation and baseline measurements, randomize participants 1:1 using an independent statistician's computer-generated sequence, stratified by site with randomly varying blocks of four and six. A secure allocation service releases assignment to the training coordinator only after eligibility and baseline measurements have been recorded. Clinic assessors cannot access the allocation list. Do not assign before consent or alter group membership according to later adherence.
design.masking_description: Masking: Single, Outcomes Assessor. Participants and the training coordinator know assignment. The clinic vision assessor is masked. This is not a double-masked study; participant-reported symptoms cannot be masked. The vision assessor performs the same measurements in both groups without access to training records or diaries. Participants are asked not to disclose assignment to that assessor. If assignment is inadvertently disclosed, record the masking breach; do not remove the participant automatically. There is no placebo, emergency unmasking procedure or concealed treatment needed for clinical safety. Clinical staff can access assignment when necessary.

procedures.methods: The training coordinator gives scheduled-break participants a printed sheet and a ten-minute explanation at Day 0: take a two-minute break away from the screen after each 30 minutes of screen use during screen-use sessions lasting at least two hours. No app, timer or screen device is supplied or tested. Usual-habits participants continue their ordinary break habits; they are not instructed to avoid breaks. Both groups complete one paper diary entry each evening from the day after randomization (Day 1) through Day 56 inclusive, about two minutes per day. Each entry records total screen-use hours and whether screen use occurred. Usual-habits participants record the number of breaks they naturally took; they are not given adherence targets. An evening entry is not a clinic visit. Day 0 has no home-diary entry. At Day 0, Day 14, Day 28 and Day 56, ask: "Over the past seven days, how severe was your average eye discomfort while using a digital screen?" The answer is 0 (no discomfort) through 10 (worst imaginable discomfort). Higher is worse. This is a study-specific single-item rating; no validation claim is supplied. Near-task satisfaction is 0 (not satisfied) to 10 (fully satisfied), asked only at Day 0, Day 28 and Day 56. Higher is better on this different scale. Distance visual acuity is binocular, with current correction, in logMAR; lower is better. No per-eye outcome or paired-eye model is specified. There are no research blood draws, saliva, genetic testing, banking, imaging, dilation, home devices, study medicines or surgical procedures.

safety.general_information: Potential research risks are temporary eye fatigue or headache from vision testing, frustration or embarrassment with questions, inconvenience from interrupting screen work and diary completion, travel burden, and loss of privacy. Participants can pause or stop testing. The break routine may be inconvenient and may not reduce discomfort. It is not a replacement for ordinary eye care. Persistent or worsening symptoms should be discussed with the study doctor; clinical concerns are referred to ordinary care. No direct benefit is promised. Results may help design future studies of screen-break routines. The alternative is ordinary care without joining; usual breaks and clinical treatments remain available regardless of participation.

confidentiality.data_handling: Collect name, contact information, signed consent, age, sex, eligibility, screen-use history, ordinary eye-care updates, assignment, visual acuity, ratings, diary records and reimbursement documentation. No date of birth, Social Security number, specimen or genetic information is collected. Each clinic keeps its identifying key separately on an access-controlled encrypted drive; signed consent and paper diaries are stored in locked research cabinets. Diary sheets carry study ID only and are returned at clinic visits. Participants are asked to keep diaries private while at home. Authorized clinic investigators/coordinators can access identifying records for study duties. The sponsor's reimbursement team receives participant name, mailing address, receipts and reimbursement amount solely to mail checks and reconcile expenses. Thus the sponsor DOES receive limited identifiable information; do not describe all sponsor access as coded-only. The sponsor's analysis team and statistician receive coded assessments, with no contact details or identity key. Authorized monitors, the IRB and legally authorized oversight bodies may inspect relevant original records for oversight. Sponsor reimbursement records are stored separately with restricted access. Study records, identity keys, diaries and reimbursement records are retained securely for seven years after administrative closeout on 31 December 2027, then destroyed unless a binding requirement requires longer retention. Authorization for new research health information ends at the final Day 56 contact or earlier written withdrawal. Retention does not extend collection. Withdraw authorization by writing to the coordinator at the enrolling site's mailing address. New research collection then stops; already collected data may remain in analyses and required oversight records. Ordinary care continues. No public individual-data sharing, data sale, unrelated future research use, genetic research, commercial specimens or specimen banking is planned.

section_contracts.title: Study Methods and Measurements
content_expectations: Explain the approved measurement activities in operational language. Connect each measure to the source-supplied assessment activities and relevant time point, such as chart abstraction, score review, device download, or questionnaire when those activities are approved. When the source gives no instrument, scoring rule, denominator, or detailed method, state only the observable activity; an endpoint restatement such as 'the endpoint will be evaluated' is not a measurement method. Group related measures without repeating the complete visit schedule or inventing details.
Do not replace supplied detail with generic clinical prose.

This section owns supplied specimen handling and results-return policies. Preserve collection/coding, transfer recipients and access limits, testing purpose, specimen destruction timing and any absolute deadline, future-use/sharing/sale/commercial restrictions, and the distinction between specimen retention and derived-data retention. Distinguish individual clinical results, research/genetic results, incidental findings and aggregate summaries, including any limits, preferences, recipients and timing. Keep routine-care referral arrangements when supplied. Preserve uncertainty; absent optional policies remain absent. For records-only research, describe only the approved existing records/specimens and results policies without adding collection or participant contact.

constraints: The Source-of-Truth is approved and source intake is closed. Do not request additional reviewer input.

Use only supplied approved evidence and applicable template/Fixed Clinical Boilerplate. Align shared population, groups, quantities, timing, procedures and outcomes across the Protocol, selected ICF and PRS narratives; preserve relationships and qualifications rather than copying wording.

Listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate is authorized only where applicable and consistent with the approved source. The approved source supersedes boilerplate; boilerplate must not expand decision-making authority, termination grounds, completion criteria, procedures, or safety obligations.

When a section lists both Fixed Clinical Boilerplate and minimum evidence, include all material source facts and only applicable, nonconflicting boilerplate; omit boilerplate clauses that would alter a source rule.

Do not invent study-specific facts, procedures, risks, benefits, safety obligations, legal promises, or regulatory claims. Routine-use and record-review studies acquire no additional visits, monitoring or follow-up commitments from boilerplate.
Preserve supplied numbered citations next to the Protocol claims they support and their bibliography linkage. Do not invent citations; ICF explanations use plain language.
Return exactly one result for every requested section ID.
Use only the drafted or fixed_boilerplate outcome. Sparse sections may use only applicable, source-consistent listed Fixed Clinical Boilerplate.
Return structured section content, not a whole document or document markup.

Write to each section's purpose and ownership. Explain each operational rule fully in its owning section; elsewhere give only the fact needed for that section and a brief reference to the owning heading. Preserve necessary identifiers, endpoint definitions, quantities, timing anchors/windows, conditions, exceptions, safety information and client consent language. Compress repeated explanations, not clinical meaning.
Use participant-facing language for ICF sections.

writing_examples illustrate prose and organization using synthetic inputs. Draft from this request's approved_source and section_contracts; example facts are never study evidence or boilerplate. Return the requested response format.
For icf.key-information-summary, draft directly from its canonical summary obligations; keep each concept concise and never copy a complete detailed-section sentence or paragraph.

For a Sterling ICF, BACKGROUND owns lens descriptions, comparative evidence, the evidence gap, and rationale. PURPOSE must be concise and limited to the purpose, hypothesis, and primary endpoint; do not restate BACKGROUND.

ICF PROCEDURES owns detailed study activities and DURATION owns timing. Do not repeat their detail in PURPOSE, ALTERNATIVE TREATMENTS, VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION/WITHDRAWAL, or the participant statement unless the Sterling Clause Contract explicitly requires it.

For Protocol sections, follow concept_ownership: explain owned concepts completely, keep brief_reference_only concepts concise, and do not re-explain do_not_restate concepts. Endpoint names, visit names and timing, identifiers, quantities, safety terms, and brief traceability cross-references may recur.

Protocol General Information is a compact synopsis; Objectives states the study purpose and objectives; Study Design owns the design, comparisons and grouped endpoint inventory. Study Methods and Measurements owns detailed measurement, exposure-counting, study-eye and historical-record selection rules; Visits and Examinations owns contact mode, timing and scheduled activities. Bias describes the purpose of controls with brief references to their methods, rather than repeating those instructions. Analysis Data Sets owns which observations enter analyses; Statistical Methodology owns calculations, models and interpretation. Retain complete methods once, using the actual owning headings for references.

Satisfy every section's content_expectations and cover every material value named by minimum_evidence, except that Section 15's source-derived table and notes carry its detailed inventory. Its adjacent prose should briefly introduce the table without restating its rows or notes.

Write standalone clinical content that serves the section purpose. Refer to the study and its procedures directly, rather than to the synopsis, approved source, or drafting process. Preserve genuine numbered instruments/forms, citations and explained footnotes; remove a suspected orphan marker only when its source context supports that interpretation. Omit self-referential filler and redundant narration. These editorial preferences are not publication gates.

Use reference_detail_target_words only as a soft compression signal; independent AI review assesses substantive completeness, and concise complete prose must not be padded, repeated, or invented to meet a length target.
Explicitly distinguish the study objective, hypothesis, and endpoints when they describe different constructs.
When the approved source does not define an instrument, scoring rule, denominator, missing-data method, date, or version, do not invent one or expose an internal source-gap note.
Do not use an evidence reference unless the returned prose or list actually contains the material fact it supports.

Every paragraph object and every list object must include at least one evidence_refs or boilerplate_refs value allowed by its section contract. If prose only introduces an already-cited list, omit that paragraph instead of returning empty reference arrays.

We are writing a clinical study protocol document.  
Your task is to generate the **Study Design and Methods** sections.

### Inputs we will provide (with descriptions):
- Study Title: The full official title of the study.

- Endpoints: The list of primary and secondary endpoints.
- Assessments Schedule: The planned assessments and their schedule.
- Number of Sites: The total number of investigational sites.
- Background: Background and significance text.
- Primary Objective: The main objective text.
- Hypothesis: The hypothesis text.

### What you need to do:
- Generate **studyDesignLong**: an expanded paragraph that integrates studyDesign, numberOfSites, endpoints, and assessmentsSchedule. Mention timepoints only if they are explicitly present in the inputs.
- Generate **methods**: describe bias minimization procedures.
- Generate **masked**: extract masking or blinding details.
- Generate **variables**: present the endpoits gropued.
- Generate **duration**: A very short description of how long will the patients in the study will bethe.
- Determine **studyArm**: Identify if the study is "single arm" or "double arm" based on the Study Design input.

### Important notes:
- Do not invent outcomes, procedures, masking, timepoints, or measurements beyond what is provided.
- Keep the tone professional, neutral, and consistent with clinical protocol style.

  "methods": "bias minimization methods",

  "variables": "endpoints in structured text",

}

=### Study Title:
A Single-Site, Randomized, Contralateral Eye Trial Comparing Active Sentry at Low IOP vs Ozil at High IOP


### Study Design:
Single site, single-masked, randomized, prospective contralateral eye study.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: The total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.  

Secondary Endpoints:  
- Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.  

Exploratory Endpoint:  
- Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.  


### Assessments Schedule:
- Preoperative: Eligibility evaluation, consent, visual acuity, slit lamp, and CCT measurement.  
- Operative (two visits): Sequential bilateral cataract surgeries with standard surgical findings recorded.  
- Postoperative Day 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring.  
- Postoperative Week 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring. 


### Timeline
Study Start Date: March 1, 2025  
First Patient In: March 15, 2025  
Last Patient Out: December 15, 2025  
Data Analysis: January 2026  
Final Report Submission: February 28, 2026


### Number of Sites:
One


### Background:
Elevated bottle height (i.e., intraocular pressure, IOP) during cataract surgery impacts corneal tissue and the anterior chamber. Previous studies found Active Sentry at 44–50 mmHg as safe and efficacious as Ozil at 65–70 mmHg, but did not test Active Sentry at lower IOP levels (20 mmHg), which is its main advantage.


### Primary Objective:
To assess the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP compared with the Ozil handpiece at high IOP.


### Hypothesis:
The Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP is non-inferior to the Ozil at high IOP in terms of surgical efficiency.

  "studyDesignLong": "This study is a single site, single-masked, randomized, prospective, contralateral eye study of the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP compared with the Ozil at high IOP. Subjects will be assessed pre-operatively, operatively, and at 1 day and 1 week post-operatively. Clinical evaluations will include measurement of visual acuity and central corneal thickness (CCT).

The primary outcome measure will be the total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.

Secondary outcome measures are as follows:
• Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.
• Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.

Exploratory outcome measures are as follows:
• Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.",
  "methods": "As a randomized study there is no expected bias. Patient selection will be based on the patient’s interest and the surgeon’s opinion as to whether they are a suitable candidate for sequential bilateral cataract surgery. The data analyzer will be masked.

The measurement of visual acuity will be conducted in a systematic fashion to minimize bias. Individuals conducting visual acuity measures will be instructed to perform the same testing in the same fashion for all subjects, with the same level of encouragement to subjects.

All data collection will be completed through provided Case Report Forms (CRFs) or computer files generated by automated test equipment. All site personnel involved in the study will be trained in regard to conducting study-specific procedures.",
  "masked": "The data analyzer will be masked.",

Secondary:
• Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.
• Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.

Exploratory:
• Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.",
  "duration": "Preoperative (≤90 days) to 1 week postoperative",
  "studyArm": "double arm"
}

=### Study Title: 
A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of CardioRelief in Patients with Stage II Hypertension


### Study Design:
This study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in patients with Stage II hypertension. The trial will involve multiple investigational sites, though the exact number is unspecified. Participants will be assessed for changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life over a 12-week period. Assessments will include vital signs at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12; laboratory tests and ECG at baseline and week 12; and a quality of life questionnaire at baseline and week 12.


### Background:
Hypertension remains one of the leading causes of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite available treatments, many patients do not achieve adequate blood pressure control. CardioRelief is a novel calcium channel blocker that has shown promising results in early-phase studies, with the potential to improve outcomes and reduce side effects compared to standard therapy.


### Primary Objective:
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in reducing systolic blood pressure in adults with Stage II hypertension over a 12-week period.


### Hypothesis:
CardioRelief will result in a statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to placebo, with fewer reported adverse events.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: Change from baseline in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks.

Secondary Endpoints: Change in diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life.


### Assessments Schedule:
Vital Signs: Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12.

Lab Tests: Complete blood count, serum electrolytes, liver function tests at baseline and week 12.

ECG: Baseline and week 12.

Quality of Life Questionnaire: Baseline and week 12.

### Timeline
Study Start Date: June 1, 2025 First Patient In: July 15, 2025 Last Patient Out: December 20, 2026 Data Analysis: January–February 2027 Final Report Submission: March 31, 2027

### Number of Sites:
One

### Study Title: 
A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of CardioRelief in Patients with Stage II Hypertension


### Study Design:
This study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in patients with Stage II hypertension. The trial will involve multiple investigational sites, though the exact number is unspecified. Participants will be assessed for changes in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life over a 12-week period. Assessments will include vital signs at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12; laboratory tests and ECG at baseline and week 12; and a quality of life questionnaire at baseline and week 12.


### Background:
Hypertension remains one of the leading causes of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite available treatments, many patients do not achieve adequate blood pressure control. CardioRelief is a novel calcium channel blocker that has shown promising results in early-phase studies, with the potential to improve outcomes and reduce side effects compared to standard therapy.


### Primary Objective:
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of CardioRelief in reducing systolic blood pressure in adults with Stage II hypertension over a 12-week period.


### Hypothesis:
CardioRelief will result in a statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to placebo, with fewer reported adverse events.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: Change from baseline in systolic blood pressure at 12 weeks.

Secondary Endpoints: Change in diastolic blood pressure, incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and patient-reported quality of life.


### Assessments Schedule:
Vital Signs: Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12.

Lab Tests: Complete blood count, serum electrolytes, liver function tests at baseline and week 12.

ECG: Baseline and week 12.

Quality of Life Questionnaire: Baseline and week 12.

Two groups. Masking: Single, Outcomes Assessor. Participants and the training coordinator know assignment. The clinic vision assessor is masked. This is not a double-masked study; participant-reported symptoms cannot be masked. Number of sites: 2, both in the United States. ### Background:

### Hypothesis:
The scheduled-break group will have a greater reduction in eye discomfort than the usual-habits group. This is an exploratory feasibility study, not a confirmatory efficacy study; benefit is not established.
